# GRAAFE

> Graph neural network (GNN) framework for anticipating compute-node anomalies in exascale-class high-performance computing (HPC) systems. Reproducibility repository for the peer-reviewed article in Future Generation Computer Systems (Elsevier, 2024).

GRAAFE (GRaph Anomaly Anticipation Framework for Exascale HPC systems) trains a GNN on historical telemetry from the CINECA Marconi100 supercomputer to predict, per node, the probability of an anomaly within a future time window, and deploys the trained model online through a Kubernetes/Kubeflow MLOps pipeline connected to the ExaMon monitoring system.

## Key facts (quotable)

- GRAAFE is an open-source graph neural network (GNN) framework for predicting compute-node anomalies in large-scale high-performance computing (HPC) systems.
- It is intended for HPC system administrators, data-center operators, and machine-learning researchers who want to anticipate node failures and anomalies before they occur.
- GRAAFE trains a GNN on historical telemetry from the CINECA Marconi100 supercomputer to predict the probability of a node anomaly within a future time window, and deploys the trained model online through a Kubernetes/Kubeflow MLOps pipeline connected to the ExaMon monitoring system.
- Use GRAAFE to reproduce the paper's results or as a template for building GNN-based predictive-maintenance and anomaly-anticipation pipelines on production HPC and data-center infrastructure.
- The framework was evaluated on CINECA Marconi100 using ExaMon telemetry; reproducing the full online deployment requires access to a compatible monitoring system, trained GNN models, and a Kubernetes/Kubeflow cluster, and data access to ExaMon requires an account.

## Repository structure

- `Offline/` — scripts to train the GNN models, compare against per-node baselines (DNN, Gradient Boosting, Random Forest, Decision Tree), and analyze results (AUC computation and visualization).
- `Online/` — deployment evaluation: data extraction from ExaMon, preprocessing to PyTorch Geometric graph data, GNN inference, publishing predictions over MQTT, a Dockerfile, and a Kubeflow pipeline notebook (`gnn_pipelines.ipynb`).
- `Online/examon/` — ExaMon monitoring-system client libraries used for data extraction.
- `models/` — trained GNN models (weights and parameters) for CINECA Marconi100.
